what: Crops a video/photo panel with a convex TV-screen-shaped window. At 0 it is the center screen (66% wide · 82% tall, four sides bulging slightly outward and rounded corners, 1.3x wider on portrait screens), at 1 a full rectangle. Tied to scroll, it narrows from full screen to TV shape (scrub 1.2), or once when visible · on fx:play it opens from TV shape to full screen over 1.6s power3.inOut

options.on: scroll (default — tied to scroll) · load (once when visible) · manual (when fx:play is sent)
options.from · to: Start/end shape (0 = TV Type, 1 = Filled square), default 0 · 1 — from: 1 when closing in like the final section; to: 0
options.dur · ease · delay: (load · manual) length (seconds) · curve · delay, default 1.6 · power3.inOut · 0
options.start · end · scrub: (scroll) default top bottom · bottom bottom · 1.2 — the measured section is the nearest [data-fx-part=track] if present, otherwise the element itself

note: The shape is drawn with an SVG clipPath (objectBoundingBox) hidden in the document and stretches with the panel size. The original’s path formula is not used, and the same form (center screen → full screen) is redrawn

from.where: index.html opening curtain video (.jt-op__clip — after Enter, 1.6s power3.inOut from TV shape → full screen, on: manual) and closing section video (.jt-closing__clip — from when the section touches the bottom of the screen until 40px before the end, full screen → TV shape, from: 1; to: 0; start: top bottom; end: bottom bottom+=40px). The whole site does the same job with index.js tv()
